items.prompt: A review card sits at step 2 and the owner rates it easy. Where does scheduleReview put it?
items.answer: Step 4, due 14 days after the server accepted the answer
distractors: Step 3, due 7 days later, since easy adds one step like good
Step 4, due 3 days later: the old step decides the interval
Step 5, due 30 days later; easy always jumps to the top step
items.explanation: easy adds two steps (clampStep(currentStep + 2)), and the interval is looked up for the ARRIVAL step: intervalDaysForStep(4) reads REVIEW_INTERVAL_DAYS[3] = 14.

items.prompt: An objectively graded review card is answered incorrectly, but the client sends the rating good. What is applied?
items.answer: again: step 0, due in 10 minutes, with ratingWasForced set to true
distractors: good, as sent; correctness is stored but never changes the schedule
hard: the step is kept and the card comes back in one day instead
The request is refused with 409, since the rating contradicts it
items.explanation: correctness === false forces the effective rating to again whatever the client sent (review-scheduler.ts:76-77); again resets to step 0 and adds REVIEW_AGAIN_DELAY_MINUTES (10). ratingWasForced is true because the sent rating was not again.

items.prompt: Three due cards: A was reviewed before and fell due yesterday, B was never reviewed and fell due last week, C was reviewed before and fell due today. In what order does orderDueQueue return them?
items.answer: A, C, B; previously reviewed cards come first, oldest due date first
distractors: B, A, C: the queue is a single list sorted by due date, oldest first
C, A, B, because the most recently due reviewed card is shown first
B, then A and C, as never-reviewed cards are introduced before others
items.explanation: orderDueQueue splits due cards into overdue (lastReviewedAt !== null) and fresh (null), sorts each by dueAt then cardId, and returns overdue before fresh. B is older but was never reviewed, so it goes last.

items.prompt: A card already at step 5 is rated good. What happens, and which entry of REVIEW_INTERVAL_DAYS is read?
items.answer: It stays at step 5, due in 30 days, because index 4 is read
distractors: It moves to step 6 and reads index 5, the final 30 in the array
It wraps around to step 0 and becomes due again in 10 minutes
It stays at step 5 but its interval doubles to 60 days each time
items.explanation: clampStep caps the step at REVIEW_MAX_STEP (5), and intervalDaysForStep reads index min(step, 5) - 1 = 4, which is 30. The sixth entry of [1, 3, 7, 14, 30, 30] is never read.

items.prompt: A concept has two clean, objectively graded passes on two different choice exercises. What is its status?
items.answer: practicing, because neither pass is application or debugging work
distractors: demonstrated: two distinct items passed with no assistance at all
retained, since both passes were graded by the server objectively
unseen; choice exercises never create evidence for a concept
items.explanation: demonstrated needs at least two distinct clean objective passes AND applicationOrDebugPasses >= 1. EXERCISE_COGNITIVE_LEVEL maps choice to recall, so the second condition fails and the concept stays practicing.

items.prompt: The owner reveals the solution for exercise e1, resets the editor, then passes e1 the next day. How is that pass recorded?
items.answer: As solution_viewed, since the reveal history of that revision is permanent
distractors: As none: resetting the editor clears the reveal flag for that item
As hints, which is how a reveal followed by an editor reset is downgraded
It is not recorded at all, since passes after a reveal are dropped
items.explanation: resolveAssistance returns solution_viewed whenever any solution reveal exists for the same (exerciseId, masteryRevision). RevealEvent rows are never deleted, so a reset changes nothing; only a new mastery revision starts a clean history.

items.prompt: A demonstrated concept gets two due, server-graded correct reviews 6 days apart. What is its status?
items.answer: Still demonstrated: the second review must come at least 7 days later
distractors: retained, as two correct due reviews on separate dates are enough
review_due, because the second review arrived ahead of schedule
practicing again; such a short gap discards the earlier review entirely
items.explanation: findRetentionPair needs two successful due reviews on separate UTC dates with the second at least RETENTION_MIN_DAYS_BETWEEN_REVIEWS (7) days after the first. Six days is not enough, so no retention pair exists.

items.prompt: A concept is demonstrated but has no retention pair yet, and its earliest card due date has passed. What does classifyConcept return?
items.answer: demonstrated, as only a retained concept turns into review_due
distractors: review_due, as any concept with an overdue card is flagged
practicing, because an overdue card withdraws the evidence
retained, and the overdue card is simply ignored until later
items.explanation: The overdue check only applies inside the branch demonstrated && retentionPair !== null (evidence.ts:178-180). A merely demonstrated concept stays demonstrated, and history is never deleted.

items.prompt: A placement attempt scores 4 of 5, but the one wrong item is flagged critical. Does the owner qualify?
items.answer: No. Every critical item must pass as well as 4 of 5 being correct
distractors: Yes; 4 of 5 meets minimumCorrect, which is the only rule applied
Yes, but the chapter is marked practiceOnly instead of placed_out
No, because placement requires all 5 items, critical or not
items.explanation: gradePlacement qualifies only when score >= minimumCorrect (4) AND, with requireAllCritical true, failedCriticalItemIds is empty. One failed critical item blocks qualification even at 4 of 5.

items.prompt: The owner already placed out of a chapter, then takes the same assessment version again and fails. What changes?
items.answer: Nothing: the retake is practiceOnly and never revokes placed_out
distractors: placed_out is revoked, since the latest attempt is the one that counts
The retake counts as fresh evidence, so the failed result replaces placed_out
The chapter drops back to in_progress until a new version is passed
items.explanation: isPracticeOnly(previousAttemptsOnVersion) is true for any earlier attempt on that version, because submitting revealed the answers. A practice attempt grants no fresh placement evidence and never revokes an existing placed_out.

items.prompt: The first passing attempt on an exercise came right after the owner revealed its solution. How much XP is granted?
items.answer: 10 XP under exercise:<id>:r<rev>, with the assistance recorded apart
distractors: None, since solution_viewed attempts are excluded from every XP award
5 XP: assisted passes earn half of the normal first-pass amount
20 XP, the same amount that a first lesson completion would have earned
items.explanation: The first-pass award (XP.exerciseFirstPass = 10, key exercise:<id>:r<masteryRevision>) is granted whether or not the attempt was assisted; assistance is shown alongside rather than punished twice.

items.prompt: Two review answers arrive at the same moment with the same expectedRevision and different clientEventIds. What can happen today?
items.answer: Both pass the revision check, and the second update applies on top of the first
distractors: The second gets 409 REVISION_CONFLICT, exactly as the A05 integration test proves
The second replays the first stored result; the two card ids match
Both fail: the transaction is SERIALIZABLE and PostgreSQL aborts each
items.explanation: The review route reads the state, compares revision, then updates keyed only on (userId, cardId) at READ COMMITTED. Both requests can pass the read; the second update waits for the row lock and then applies. The A05 test sends its requests one after the other, so it does not cover this race; notes use a conditional updateMany instead.

items.front: The four conditions for a concept to be demonstrated
items.back: 1) two passing attempts graded server_objective or browser_automated; 2) on distinct item ids; 3) assistance none on both; 4) at least one is application (function) or debugging (code-reading), not recall (choice, predict-output). Self-assessed work never counts.

items.front: What retained adds on top of demonstrated
items.back: Two reviews that were due when answered, graded correct by server_objective, on separate UTC dates, the second at least 7 days after the first. Self-rated free-recall reviews are counted apart (selfRatedReviewCount) and never satisfy retention.

items.front: The four review ratings and their effect on step and due date
items.back: again: step 0, due in 10 minutes. hard: step unchanged, due in 1 day. good: step + 1 (max 5), due per the ladder 1/3/7/14/30 days. easy: step + 2 (max 5), due per the ladder. Intervals are measured from server acceptance time.

items.front: version++ versus masteryRevision++ on a ContentVersion
items.back: A typo or clearer wording bumps version only, and existing evidence stands. A change to required behaviour, grading cases, objectives or solution bumps masteryRevision: prior evidence stays visible, and new practice earns its own evidence. A version number is never reused with different bytes.
